title: Template literals
description: Backtick strings with ${expr} interpolation, real multi-line support, and tagged-template hooks for custom processing.

notes: Use backticks (`), not single or double quotes — only backticks enable ${} and multi-line.
Escape a literal backtick with \` and a literal $ with \$ when needed.
Tagged templates are rarely used in app code; you will see them in libraries (styled-components, GraphQL gql).

questions.explain: Only backticks parse ${...}. Inside single or double quotes it stays literal text — and you lose real multi-line too, since backticks buy both.

Any expression — the reference interpolates 2 + 3 and name.toUpperCase(), not just bare identifiers. Statements are the limit: if or for inside ${} is a SyntaxError, so ternaries are how you branch there.
A newline typed between backticks IS a newline in the value — the reference's block literal spans three lines with no escapes. No mode or tag is required; that is plain template-literal behaviour.

questions.q: What is the type of an untagged template literal expression?
options: Whatever the literal's first interpolated expression evaluates to
questions.explain: Interpolation runs immediately and every value is stringified, so the result is a plain string whatever you embed. Only a TAG function ever sees the strings array and the values separately — and a tag can return any type it likes.

exercises.prompt: Compute and embed an expression inside the template.
Method calls inside ${} — fill the two methods to uppercase and to repeat.

L3.prompt: Write `greet(user)` returning "Hi <name>, you have <msgs> messages." using a template literal. Log `greet({ name: "Ada", msgs: 3 })`.
hints: Two ${} slots — one for name, one for msgs.
